title: Block Permutation
description: Defines conditional component overrides based on block state values using Molang conditions. When the condition evaluates true, the permutation's components replace or merge with base components. Enables blocks that change appearance or behavior based on direction, power state, age, or custom properties.

block_components_connection_rule.title: Block Components Connection Rule
block_components_connection_rule.description: Defines whether other blocks such as fences, walls, bars, and glass panes are allowed to connect to this block.

accepts_connections_from.title: Connection Type
accepts_connections_from.description: The type of block allowed to connect to this block. Note that the "only_fences" option allows connections from all Vanilla fences excluding NetherBrick.

enabled_directions.title: Enabled Directions
enabled_directions.description: The cardinal directions that connection is enabled for. Note that if "none" is specified for "accepts_connections_from", this field will not be used.

block_components_crafting_table.title: Block Components Crafting Table
block_components_crafting_table.description: Makes your block into a custom crafting table which enables the crafting table UI and the ability to craft recipes.

crafting_tags.title: Crafting Tags
crafting_tags.description: Defines the tags recipes should define to be crafted on this table. Limited to 64 tags. Each tag is limited to 64 characters.

table_name.title: Table Name
table_name.description: Specifies the language file key that maps to what text will be displayed in the UI of this table. If the string given can not be resolved as a loc string, the raw string given will be displayed. If this field is omitted, the name displayed will default to the name specified in the "display_name" component. If this block has no "display_name" component, the name displayed will default to the name of the block.

block_components_item_specific_speed.title: Block Components Item Specific Speed
block_components_item_specific_speed.description: Defines mining speed for a specific item.

destroy_speed.title: Destroy Speed
destroy_speed.description: Mining speed for that specific item. A negative number means the block can't be mined with that item.

item.title: Item
item.description: The item with a specific mining speed.

block_components_destruction_particles.title: Block Components Destruction Particles
block_components_destruction_particles.description: Sets the particles that will be used when block is destroyed. This component can be omitted.

particle_count.title: Particle Count
particle_count.description: Sets number of particles to spawn on block destruction.

texture.title: Texture
texture.description: The texture name used for the particle.

tint_method.title: Tint Method
tint_method.description: Sets the tint method of the particle. Tint method logic varies, but often refers to the "rain" and "temperature" of the biome the block is placed in to compute the tint. Supported tint methods are "none", "default_foliage", "birch_foliage", "evergreen_foliage", "dry_foliage", "grass" and "water"

block_components_embedded_visual.title: Block Components Embedded Visual
block_components_embedded_visual.description: This defines how a block embedded into an other block renders. Eg. a block in a flowerpot.

bone_visibility.title: Bone Visibility
bone_visibility.description: A JSON object that contains a list of key/value pairs that map from bone name in the specified geometry file (key) to a Molang expression that tells whether the bone should be visible or not (value). The expression is limited to using the "query.block_state()" query. When using "bone_visibility" in geometry components in the "permutations" section, you must also have a default version of the geometry component with "bone_visibility" in the "components" section.

culling.title: Culling
culling.description: Which block_culling .json file to use when rendering this block.

culling_layer.title: Culling Layer
culling_layer.description: A string that allows culling rule to group multiple blocks together when comparing them. When using the minecraft namespace, the only allowed culling layer identifiers are : "minecraft:culling_layer.undefined" or "minecraft:culling_layer.leaves". When using no namespaces or a custom one, the names must start and end with an alpha-numeric character.

culling_shape.title: Culling Shape
culling_shape.description: Currently only available with the VoxelShape experiment on. The voxel shape used for culling adjacent block faces. Voxel shapes work together with culling rules and will not function if there is no culling rule defined for the block. Only adjacent blocks with voxel shapes will occlude using this shape. Blocks using \"minecraft:geometry.full_block\" always use the unit cube shape and will ignore custom shapes if specified. When using the minecraft namespace, the only currently available culling shape identifiers are : \"minecraft:empty\" or \"minecraft:unit_cube\". When using no namespaces or a custom one, the names must start and end with an alpha-numeric character.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The description identifier of the geometry to use to render this block. This identifier must either match an existing geometry identifier in any of the loaded resource packs or be one of the currently supported Vanilla identifiers: "minecraft:geometry.full_block" or "minecraft:geometry.cross".

uv_lock.title: Uv Lock
uv_lock.description: A field that is either a Boolean or an array of strings, max size 64 strings. This field locks UV orientation for all/some bones in the geometry, regardless of how the block is rotated using "minecraft:transformation" component. For performance reasons it's recommended to use the Boolean.

can_contain_liquid.title: Can Contain Liquid
can_contain_liquid.description: Whether this block can contain the liquid. For example, if the liquid type is `water`, this means the block can be waterlogged.

liquid_type.title: Liquid Type
liquid_type.description: The type of liquid this detection rule is for. Currently, `water` is the only supported liquid type. If this field is omitted, `water` will be the liquid type by default.

on_liquid_touches.title: Liquid Reaction
on_liquid_touches.description:
How the block reacts to flowing water. Must be one of the following options:
"blocking" - The default value for this field. The block stops the liquid from flowing.
"broken" - The block is destroyed completely.
"popped" - The block is destroyed and its item is spawned.
"no_reaction" - The block is unaffected; visually, the liquid will flow through the block.

stops_liquid_flowing_from_direction.title: Stops Liquid Flowing From Direction
stops_liquid_flowing_from_direction.description: When a block contains a liquid, controls the directions in which the liquid can't flow out from the block. Also controls the directions in which a block can stop liquid flowing into it if `no_reaction` is set for the `on_liquid_touches` field. Can be a list of the following directions: "up", "down", "north", "south", "east", "west". The default is an empty list; this means that liquid can flow out of all directions by default.

use_liquid_clipping.title: Use Liquid Clipping
use_liquid_clipping.description: Whether this block uses the encompassing collider to visually clip the liquid. The encompassing collider is the smallest single AABB that contains all of the block's colliders.

block_components_liquid_detection.title: Block Components Liquid Detection
block_components_liquid_detection.description: The definitions for how a block behaves when detecting liquid. Only one rule definition is allowed per liquid type - if multiple are specified, the first will be used and the rest will be ignored.

detection_rules.title: Detection Rules
detection_rules.description:
Properties:
• can_contain_liquid (boolean) = false
• liquid_type (string) = water
• on_liquid_touches (string) = blocking
• stops_liquid_flowing_from_direction (object) = []
• use_liquid_clipping (boolean) = false

block_components_movable.title: Block Components Movable
block_components_movable.description: This defines how a block reacts to being moved by another block like a piston.

movement_type.title: Movement Type
movement_type.description: How the block reacts to being pushed by another block like a piston. The options are: "push_pull" - The default value for this field. The block will be pushed and pulled by a piston. "push" - The block will only be pulled by a piston and will ignore a sticky piston. "popped" - The block is destroyed when moved by a piston. "immovable" - The block is unaffected by a piston.

sticky.title: Sticky Type
sticky.description: How the block should handle adjacent blocks around it when being pushed by another block like a piston. The options are: "same" - Adjacent blocks to this block will be moved when moved. This excludes other blocks with the "same" property. This will only work with the movement_type: "push_pull". "none" - The default and will not move adjacent blocks.

block_components_random_offset.title: Block Components Random Offset
block_components_random_offset.description:
This component defines a random offset for the block, seeded based on the block's position and the specified range and steps. It affects the block's rendered position, outline, and collision.
If the random offset causes the collision box to extend beyond the bounds of a cube, the offset range will automatically adjust to keep the collision box within the cube.
Culling for this block is performed without considering the random offset.

allows_wire_to_step_down.title: Allows Wire To Step Down
allows_wire_to_step_down.description: Specifies if redstone wire can stair-step downward on the block.

redstone_conductor.title: Redstone Conductor
redstone_conductor.description: Specifies if the block can be powered by redstone.

block_components_redstone_consumer.title: Block Components Redstone Consumer
block_components_redstone_consumer.description: A component describing how a block can consume and potentially propagate a redstone signal. This component is not available for block permutations.

min_power.title: Min Power
min_power.description: Optional minimum value for incoming signal strength. If signal strength is greater than or equal to this value then the 'onRedstoneUpdate' event is sent to Scripts. Defaults to 0 meaning event is always emitted.

propagates_power.title: Propagates Power
propagates_power.description: Optional Boolean to control whether a signal can pass through this block or not, defaults to false.

block_components_redstone_producer.title: Block Components Redstone Producer
block_components_redstone_producer.description: The definitions for how a block can produce a redstone signal.

connected_faces.title: Connected Faces
connected_faces.description:
The list of faces that are considered connected to the circuit. If a face is not connected, it will not provide power to the block touching that face.
By default, all faces are connected.

power.title: Power
power.description: The strength of the redstone signal produced by this block. 0 means no signal and higher numbers mean stronger signal.

strongly_powered_face.title: Facing
strongly_powered_face.description:
The block touching this face will become strongly powered with the signal level strength of "power".
Strongly powered blocks will power adjacent blocks.
By default, the block will not strongly power any face.

transform_relative.title: Transform Relative
transform_relative.description: If true, the "strongly_powered_face" and "connected_faces" properties will be rotated according to the "minecraft:transformation" component.

block_components_support.title: Block Components Support
block_components_support.description: Defines the support shape of the block. Currently only allows for blocks to have the same shape as a Vanilla fence and Vanilla stair. To work with custom stairs, requires the use of "minecraft:vertical_half" and "minecraft:cardinal_direction" or "minecraft:facing_direction" which can be set through the "minecraft:placement_direction" block trait. Custom blocks without this component will default to unit cube support. The type of support shape for this block. Currently, the options are: "fence" and "stair".

shape.title: Support Shape
shape.description: Required field. The type of support shape for this block.

block_components_tick.title: Block Components Tick
block_components_tick.description: Defines tick interval behavior for a block.

interval_range.title: Interval Range
interval_range.description: A range of values, specified in ticks, that will be used to decide the interval between times this block will tick. Each interval will be chosen randomly from the range, so the times between this block ticking will differ given an interval_range of two different values. If the values in the interval_range are the same, the block will always be ticked after that number of ticks.
interval_range.x-runtime-constraint-description: The first value must be equal or lower than the second value

looping.title: Looping
looping.description: Does the block tick continuously? If false, the block will only be ticked once, after a delay equal to a number of ticks randomly chosen from the interval_range. If true, the block will loop, and each interval between ticks will be equal to a number of ticks randomly chosen from the interval_range.

catch_chance_modifier.title: Catch Chance Modifier
catch_chance_modifier.description: A modifier affecting the chance that this block will catch flame when next to a fire. Values are greater than or equal to 0, with a higher number meaning more likely to catch on fire. For a catch_chance_modifier greater than 0, the fire will continue to burn until the block is destroyed (or it will burn forever if the destroy_chance_modifier is 0). If the catch_chance_modifier is 0, and the block is directly ignited, the fire will eventually burn out without destroying the block (or it will have a chance to be destroyed if destroy_chance_modifier is greater than 0). The default value of 5 is the same as that of Planks.

destroy_chance_modifier.title: Destroy Chance Modifier
destroy_chance_modifier.description: A modifier affecting the chance that this block will be destroyed by flames when on fire. Values are greater than or equal to 0, with a higher number meaning more likely to be destroyed by fire. For a destroy_chance_modifier of 0, the block will never be destroyed by fire, and the fire will burn forever if the catch_chance_modifier is greater than 0. The default value of 20 is the same as that of Planks.

bone_visibility.title: Bone Visibility
bone_visibility.description: A JSON object that contains a list of key/value pairs that map from bone name in the specified geometry file (key) to a Molang expression that tells whether the bone should be visible or not (value). The expression is limited to using the "query.block_state()" query. When using "bone_visibility" in geometry components in the "permutations" section, you must also have a default version of the geometry component with "bone_visibility" in the "components" section.

culling.title: Culling
culling.description: Which block_culling .json file to use when rendering this block.

culling_layer.title: Culling Layer
culling_layer.description: A string that allows culling rule to group multiple blocks together when comparing them. When using the minecraft namespace, the only allowed culling layer identifiers are : "minecraft:culling_layer.undefined" or "minecraft:culling_layer.leaves". When using no namespaces or a custom one, the names must start and end with an alpha-numeric character.

culling_shape.title: Culling Shape
culling_shape.description: Currently only available with the VoxelShape experiment on. The voxel shape used for culling adjacent block faces. Voxel shapes work together with culling rules and will not function if there is no culling rule defined for the block. Only adjacent blocks with voxel shapes will occlude using this shape. Blocks using \"minecraft:geometry.full_block\" always use the unit cube shape and will ignore custom shapes if specified. When using the minecraft namespace, the only currently available culling shape identifiers are : \"minecraft:empty\" or \"minecraft:unit_cube\". When using no namespaces or a custom one, the names must start and end with an alpha-numeric character.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The description identifier of the geometry to use to render this block. This identifier must either match an existing geometry identifier in any of the loaded resource packs or be one of the currently supported Vanilla identifiers: "minecraft:geometry.full_block" or "minecraft:geometry.cross".

uv_lock.title: Uv Lock
uv_lock.description: A field that is either a Boolean or an array of strings, max size 64 strings. This field locks UV orientation for all/some bones in the geometry, regardless of how the block is rotated using "minecraft:transformation" component. For performance reasons it's recommended to use the Boolean.

minecraft:geometry.title: Minecraft Geometry
minecraft:geometry.description: The component that describes the geometry to use to render this block. It can be specified as a JSON object with the following fields, or simply as a string containing the description identifier of the geometry to use to render this block. This identifier must either match an existing geometry identifier in any of the loaded resource packs or be one of the currently supported Vanilla identifiers: "minecraft:geometry.full_block" or "minecraft:geometry.cross".

tint_method.title: Tint Method
tint_method.description: Sets the tint method of the block when rendered to a map. Tint method logic varies, but often refers to the "rain" and "temperature" of the biome the block is placed in to compute the tint. Supported tint methods are "none", "default_foliage", "birch_foliage", "evergreen_foliage", "dry_foliage", "grass" and "water"

Limited to 64 instances.

minecraft:random_offset.title: Minecraft Random Offset
minecraft:random_offset.description:
This component defines a random offset for the block, seeded based on the block's position and the specified range and steps. It affects the block's rendered position, outline, and collision.
If the random offset causes the collision box to extend beyond the bounds of a cube, the offset range will automatically adjust to keep the collision box within the cube.
Culling for this block is performed without considering the random offset.

• y (object) = {"range":{"max":0,"m
• z (object) = {"range":{"max":0,"m

To work with custom stairs, requires the use of "minecraft:vertical_half" and "minecraft:cardinal_direction" or "minecraft:facing_direction" which can be set through the "minecraft:placement_direction" block trait. Custom blocks without this component will default to unit cube support. The type of support shape for this block. Currently, the options are: "fence" and "stair".
